statement: What is the sum of all the numbers $x$ that satisfy $\bigl|\,x - |2x - 6|\,\bigr| = 3$?

choices.misconception: I only worked on the case $x < 3$, where $|2x - 6| = 6 - 2x$, kept its solution $x = 1$, and never tried the case $x \ge 3$.
I dropped the outer absolute value bars and solved $x - |2x - 6| = 3$, which has only the solution $x = 3$.
I replaced $|2x - 6|$ by $6 - 2x$ for every $x$, solved $|3x - 6| = 3$ to get $x = 1$ and $x = 3$, and added them, missing $x = 9$.
I replaced $|2x - 6|$ by $2x - 6$ for every $x$, solved $|6 - x| = 3$ to get $x = 3$ and $x = 9$, and missed the solution $x = 1$.

hints: Remove the inner absolute value first by splitting into the cases $x \ge 3$ and $x < 3$.
If $x \ge 3$, then $|2x - 6| = 2x - 6$ and the equation becomes $|6 - x| = 3$. If $x < 3$, it becomes $|3x - 6| = 3$.
Solve each case and keep only the solutions that fit that case's condition. Do not count the same solution twice.

solutions.reliable: If $x \ge 3$, then $|2x - 6| = 2x - 6$ and $x - (2x - 6) = 6 - x$, so the equation is $|6 - x| = 3$, giving $x = 3$ or $x = 9$. Both satisfy $x \ge 3$. If $x < 3$, then $|2x - 6| = 6 - 2x$ and $x - (6 - 2x) = 3x - 6$, so the equation is $|3x - 6| = 3$, giving $x = 1$ or $x = 3$. Only $x = 1$ satisfies $x < 3$ (and $x = 3$ was already found). The solutions are $1$, $3$ and $9$, and their sum is $13$. Check $x = 1$: $|1 - 4| = 3$.
